specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: 6. Authorization is deny-by-default and evaluated on every executable backend boundary. Hiding UI rows is a projection behavior, never the security boundary.

- root, system, namespace-owner, database-owner, and other privileged SurrealDB sessions MUST NOT execute ordinary protected-resource flows or count as privacy/isolation proof because privileged users bypass table permissions;

Application authorization remains required for action semantics and capability checks; record-user table/field permissions plus ResourceBroker are the non-bypassable product data boundary, not the only policy layer.

**[LM-RLS-001]** Multi-user workspace isolation MUST use authenticated record-user table/field permissions intersected with ResourceBroker scope. A `viewer` can read but not create/edit LoomBlocks; a `member` can create and edit; an `admin` can delete and manage workspace settings.

**[LM-RLS-002]** Authority tables default to `PERMISSIONS NONE`; every grant is explicit at the database layer and rechecked by ResourceBroker. Privacy proof MUST execute as authenticated record users because root, namespace, database, and other system users bypass record-user table permissions.

Deny by default (unconditional, no decision needed): every route in scope.routes rejects a caller without a valid account session + live channel binding with the constant denial BEFORE touching any table, filesystem path, DuckDB store or process. This includes the Atelier routes (api/atelier.rs:300-1104 @2f49f2a6), locus, preferences, calendar, stage, canvases, knowledge CRDT/ingestion/memory/retrieval and GET /kernel/trace_projection.

Workspace-scoped tables (canvases, canvas_nodes, canvas_edges, calendar_sources, calendar_events, calendar_activity_spans, calendar_mutation_outbox, stage_capture_artifacts, knowledge_source_roots and ingestion children, kernel_crdt_updates/snapshots/denial receipts, knowledge memory/retrieval tables, preference_records/receipts with scope_kind='workspace'): the route authorizes against the workspace resource (Read+fs.read for reads, Update/Create+fs.write for writes, Delete+fs.write for deletes; fr.read for Flight Recorder reads) and every read/write runs inside with_record_user_scope; schema.surql gives each table per-operation predicates via fn::mt109_has_workspace_access(record::id(workspace_id), <action>, <cap>) instead of PERMISSIONS NONE. calendar events must no longer read other accounts' loom_blocks (calendar_activity.rs:224 @2f49f2a6).

Account-global surfaces without a workspace or owner column (atelier_* tables, work_packets/micro_tasks, preference_records with scope_kind 'global'/'surface', atelier_stealth_*): AC-154-2 applies now; per-row account isolation is decision-gated by D-154-3 (ownership model). Until decided, these routes must not read or write rows as root on behalf of a user beyond what AC-154-2 already requires, and the residual is recorded in residual_risks with the table list. PUT /atelier/intake/items/:id/loom-projection (atelier/intake.rs:1362 @2f49f2a6) must additionally authorize loom_block read on the target block (it currently lets any account make another account's workspace undeletable).

Receipts: every kernel_event_ledger receipt these routes append (preference_record_changed, calendar, stage, canvas, ingestion, CRDT, retrieval/memory ledger appends in knowledge_memory.rs:203 and knowledge_retrieval.rs:215 @2f49f2a6) is written inside the record-user scope by a receipt predicate branch with $session = $auth.id, and carries the session principal as actor - never a header-supplied or System actor. C2 risk closed: after a preference write, the owner reads the preference_record aggregate via GET /kernel/events/aggregates/preference_record/:id and sees the new receipt; another account sees 0 receipts.

Workspace delete residuals (scope.routes[0].mt154_residual a-c): an owner's DELETE /workspaces/:id succeeds when the workspace holds calendar, stage and canvas rows created through the scoped routes; the fems_workspace_write_anchors guard statement is not dropped by the `.lines().skip(2)` slice; the Flight Recorder purge runs only after authorization and only for the deleted workspace. Extends the Operator decision 2026-09-22 (owner/admin workspace delete cascades documents, versions and Canvas boards with an audit event) exactly as C2 extended it to Loom entities and Atelier projections.

spec_resolution.ruling: Account-owned ProtectedResource. Batch all these schema edits with the other MT-154 schema changes in one re-pin. Isolation proof: account B cannot list/read/update/delete account A's rows, including through counts/search/errors.

engine_facts: SurrealDB is pinned =3.2.0 (src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml). Facts verified in surrealdb-core-3.2.0 source by the authority matrix:

F1 Table and field permissions are OFF inside a PERMISSIONS predicate (dbs/options.rs:201 new_for_permission_predicate; doc/check.rs:457-470; exec/permission.rs:87-99). Predicates and the fn::* functions they call see every row and field, including fields that are FOR select NONE.

F2 A top-level query issued on a record-user connection DOES enforce field permissions. Never probe a predicate by running `RETURN fn::...` directly as the record user; it reads permission-hidden fields as NONE and lies. Probe inside a predicate instead (e.g. a probe table whose PERMISSIONS FOR select calls the function).

F3 A denied CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE is SILENTLY IGNORED: no row returned, no error (doc/check.rs:457,469 IgnoreError::Ignore). Every record-user write MUST check the returned row (or a follow-up SELECT) and map an empty result to the constant denial; the failure otherwise surfaces later as a field ASSERT 500, an empty 404, or a guard THROW 403.

F4 REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE/UNSET and DEFINE EVENT bodies run with permissions OFF (doc/purge.rs:376,385; doc/event.rs:52,80). Cascades are never blocked by the caller's delete permission, and cascade targets need no delete predicate for the cascade itself.

F5 Session selection: `SurrealStorage::with_record_user_scope(scope, fut)` (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal.rs:956 @ab618f46) sets a tokio task-local; `with_data_operation` then signs a cloned client in as the record user. Anything outside that scope, INCLUDING work moved into `tokio::spawn`, runs as root. Re-enter the scope inside every spawned future that touches protected tables.
authority_toolkit: Rust authorization entry points (all @ab618f46, src/backend/handshake_core/src/): `api::authority::authorize_request(state, headers, capability_id, ResourceKind, external_resource_id, ResourceAction)` (api/authority.rs:1216) returns an AuthorizedResourceContext whose `.record_user_scope` MUST then wrap the storage call via `state.surreal.with_record_user_scope(ctx.record_user_scope, fut)`. A route that calls authorize_request but writes outside that scope is still ROOT-WRITE.

`api::authority::require_authenticated_session` (api/authority.rs:1013) is the axum route_layer middleware C2 used for process-starting routes with no protected-resource row (see api/debug_adapter.rs:183-186 route_layer). `authenticated_session_credentials` (api/authority.rs:1031) returns the LocalSessionContext + token + channel binding hash. Missing/invalid credentials map to `constant_denial()` = 403 {"error":"HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE"}.

schema_repin_procedure: Schema re-pin procedure (the one C2 used for MT-109 remediation_v24 and C3 is using now): (1) Batch every schema edit for this MT first. Edit `src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql` (the live schema for a fresh store). (2) For every changed statement add a (current_text, predecessor_text) pair to a delta array in `schema.rs` next to `MT109_C2_SCHEMA_DELTAS` (schema.rs:1991 @ab618f46) so predecessor reconstructions revert it and upgrades re-emit it from SCHEMA; the pair must be byte-exact (scripts in ../Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-012/MT-109/kb-c2/scripts/strip_check.js show how C2 proved a revert is exact). (3) Build the lib once, then run ONE pin-measure run of the pin tests (check PIN-MEASURE). It is expected to fail and prints the new values: MT109_LOOM_CATALOG_SHA256=, MT109_CURRENT_AUTHORITY_INFO_SHA256=, MT109_PREDECESSOR_AUTHORITY_INFO_SHA256=, MT139_CURRENT_SCHEMA_INFO_SHA256=, EXPECTED_ATELIER_CATALOG_SHA256= and the `left:` values of the GENERATED/DECLARATIVE assertions. (4) Update the pins in schema.rs: GENERATED_SURREALQL_SHA256 (:2128), DECLARATIVE_SCHEMA_CATALOG_SHA256 (:2144), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_INFO_SHA256 (:2190), EXPECTED_ATELIER_CATALOG_SHA256 (:2201) and the MT109 Loom/authority catalog pins the tests name. (5) ONE confirm run (check PIN-CONFIRM). The pin-measure run is a measurement, not an attempt; the confirm run counts against attempt_budget. Re-measure once per batch, never once per edit.

NEVER re-pin a PREDECESSOR constant (PRE_*_GENERATED_SHA256 / PRE_*_INFO_SHA256 / PREDECESSOR_*) to a newly observed value: those record historical catalogs that real on-disk stores carry; re-pinning them would make the upgrade path accept a catalog no real store has (proof laundering).

minimum_controls: Every positive proof runs as an authenticated record user (account session + channel binding). A root/admin session (with_admin_operation, test_admin_query*, SurrealStorage without with_record_user_scope) may only SEED preconditions that the product itself cannot create, and never counts as privacy/isolation proof (02:2773, LM-RLS-002).

Every changed route has: anonymous negative (no session headers), cross-account negative (a second OwnerSession cannot read or write the first account's rows, and the rows are unchanged afterwards), and where a write is involved, a read-only (viewer) negative when the grant model can express one.
Denied writes are proven by re-reading the canonical row after the call (F3: denied writes are silent). A 403 status alone is not proof that nothing was written.

Anti-scaffold: no new abstraction, trait, feature flag, config knob or helper that is not called by product code in this MT; no `#[ignore]`, no `return Ok(())` skip paths, no assertion weakened or deleted to go green; tests may not assert only on mocks/fixtures the Coder authored for a resource-boundary claim (CODER-PROOF-004, CODER-CODE-006).

No fixture-only proof: each acceptance item is proven against the real embedded SurrealDB store (fresh Handshake-managed RocksDB/SurrealKV directory under the owner runtime root), through the real axum router, with the real ResourceBroker.

Every test binary run must report a NONZERO executed count for the named tests (`running N tests` with N equal to the number of names passed with --exact); a `0 passed` result is a failure of the check, not a pass.
The drain fix changes product code under src/; the test file diff for test_app_host_mount.rs may only add diagnostics output, never relax an assertion.
